prerequisites: basic knowledge for explaining and interpreting various concepts and processes associated with the fundamental field of engineering sciences

learning_outcomes.text: Knows the basic notions, principles, techniques, and methods of economic engineering.
Understands the structure and functioning of economic-engineering systems.
Is familiar with concepts such as strategic business unit, organizational dynamics, firms and organizations in an economic and technological context.
Knows the procedures used in analyzing and solving problems in the field of economic engineering.
Efficiently applies the methods and techniques specific to economic engineering for organizational analysis and diagnosis.
Uses appropriate criteria and methods for evaluating the management of design, manufacturing, or maintenance activities.
Implements specific procedures for solving economic-engineering problems.
Writes and presents studies, assignments, and practical applications specific to the field.
Is capable of executing professional tasks according to a predefined work plan under qualified guidance.
Takes responsibility for the correct application of economic analysis and evaluation methods in engineering activities.
Actively participates in formulating efficient and ethical organizational solutions.
Achieves personal and professional development by efficiently utilizing personal resources and modern study tools.
Easily integrates into a work team, assuming specific roles within the team.
Has the capacity to autonomously propose and apply economic-engineering solutions for real problems in industry or services.

syllabus_topics: Economic and technological framework of the strategic business unit system, firm, organization
Sociological and psychological dynamics of the organization
Enterprise, firm, organization and economic-engineering contacts
Identification, formulation, and evaluation of the problem
Solving the problem by following the economic engineering analysis procedure
teaching_methods: Interactive lectures, supported by multimedia presentations, graphics, economic models, and practical examples relevant for the technical-economic analysis of mechanical systems and production processes
Explanation, demonstration, comparative analysis, study of the impact of technical solutions on costs, efficiency, competitiveness
Guided discussions, practical work, and numerical exercises
Calculation of production costs, investment evaluation, risk analysis, use of software tools for economic modeling and optimization scenario simulation

assessment_methods.method: Formative evaluation test (checks during the semester)
Active participation in seminar activities; seminar evaluation test

assessment_rules: The final evaluation result for a discipline is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity. Grades are awarded on a scale from 1 to 10, with a minimum passing grade of 5, which certifies the achievement of minimum learning outcomes and the granting of corresponding study credits. A minimum score of 5 is required for both the Exam component and the Seminar component.
